audit.whatIsWrong: Five of seven chart rows print a side their own explanation contradicts. Both layers read Skill / Fiora / Fiora / Skill / Skill / Fiora / Fiora. whys[0] says 'You own level 1' (Fiora, printed Skill); whys[1] says 'Camille spikes at 2' (Camille, printed Fiora); whys[2] says 'short trades through level 3 go her way' (Camille, printed Fiora); whys[3] says 'Levels 4-5 stay hers' (Camille, printed Skill); whys[5] says 'First item is a coin-flip' (Skill, printed Fiora).
audit.why: The packet levelChart agrees with the prose on every one of those five rows: Fiora / Camille / Camille / Camille / Skill / Skill.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Fiora 7 / Camille 4 / Camille 4 / Camille 4 / Skill 5 / Skill 5 / Camille 4 in both layers, with all seven phases[].why rewritten to state their new side.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why said Grand Challenge 'wins any committed duel' and phases[5].why said 'Ravenous Hydra is your spike — force fights the moment it completes', neither of which matches the even/coin-flip verdict the content layer gives those two rows.
audit.why: Level 6 is a mutual ult-read (The Hextech Ultimatum anchors you into a 1v1 you cannot walk out of, against a four-Vital Grand Challenge on 110s), and first item is Trinity Force resets against Profane Hydra splitpush. Both are genuinely even, not Fiora windows.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why and phases[5].why now describe the actual trade each row represents.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer names no cooldowns and never states the single interaction that decides the level 2-5 stretch: Adaptive Defenses shields Camille against the damage TYPE that hit her, so Fiora's physical autos generate the exact shield that blunts them. dontsFull bodies also do not match their own titles ('Waste W on her Q', 'Fight near walls', 'Get E-stunned' all carry the same generic filler).
audit.why: Hookshot is 16s at rank 1 and must anchor to a wall — fighting in the open lane removes her engage entirely, which is the concrete rule the page never gives. Precision Protocol (9s at rank 1) is an auto-attack reset, so the tell is the wind-up, not a cast. Tactical Sweep's outer half heals her, which is the real reason to buy Executioner's Calling.
audit.corrected: Written into breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t, report[8].t, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d and dontsFull[0..2].d.

audit.why: The kit file flags The Hextech Ultimatum as both 'channel — interruptible' and 'untargetable', and the missing-interactions file accordingly suggests telling the player that Riposte cancels her R outright and that she dodges burst through it. Riot's own description says only that she dashes to a target champion and anchors them to the area, with bonus magic damage on her attacks — no channel, no untargetability. Per the rule that the description beats a derived flag, I wrote NEITHER claim. The mirror audit reached the same conclusion.

notes: The kit file's flags on The Hextech Ultimatum (channel/interruptible and untargetable) contradict Riot's description of it, which is a dash plus an anchoring zone. The missing-interactions file wanted me to write 'your Riposte cancels her R outright' and 'she can go untargetable through your commit' on the strength of those flags. I wrote neither — both would be a fabricated mechanic on a live page, and the mirror audit independently classed them as tooltip-parse misfires. Worth a hand check. The packet's two suspectNames are near-misses on the article only ('Hextech Ultimatum' vs Riot's 'The Hextech Ultimatum'); the text reads naturally as written and I did not spend edits on it. Row 6 of the chart is the one place I departed from the packet — see questionsForUser.
